scope: Corollary 2.3 (Fibers, composition, and a fixed base) of the manuscript “Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity” (preprints/Orbifold-and-logarithmic-Iitaka-subadditivity-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b143366cc99615e1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let p : (Z′, Γ′) → (Z, Γ) be a modification with the boundary rule of Theorem 2.1. Then: (i) If p is a modification over a fixed base, it induces a logarithmic modification on a very general smooth fiber. The log Kodaira dimensions of the corresponding fibers agree. (ii) A finite composition of such modifications again has boundary equal to the strict transform of the initial boundary plus the reduced exceptional divisor of the composite. (iii) If g : (Z, Γ) → T has smooth base and g′ = g ◦ p, then (2.6) B(g′ , Γ′ ) = B(g, Γ).
